data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III report (“Creative Minds, Creative Schools”) summarises system-level and student-level patterns related to creative thinking and related contextual factors, alongside broader PISA performance trends. The excerpt states that nearly 700 000 students from 81 OECD member and partner economies took PISA 2022, and that the study is designed to measure performance, well-being, and equity before and after COVID-19 disruptions. The report discusses changes in mean performance between 2018 and 2022 (e.g., declines in reading and mathematics) and highlights relationships between technology use, teacher support, parental engagement, and mathematics performance, including references to OECD averages and point differences. It also notes that performance declines cannot be attributed solely to COVID-19, as negative trends were already present prior to 2018 in several systems. However, the excerpt does not provide the technical details needed to extract PV handling, missing-data procedures, or the exact statistical/ML models used for each reported relationship.
